electric power steering eps explained 1 steering wheel this is where everything begins when the driver turns the steering wheel a rotational force known as torque is applied in an electric power steering eps system this force does not directly move the wheels on its own instead it sends a signal to sensors and the electronic control unit ecu to provide power assist this is why steering feels light at low speeds such as when parking and remains stable at high speeds 2 torque sensor the torque sensor measures the force with which you turn the wheel and the direction of rotation left or right its job detect steering input send an electronic signal to the ecu decide how much assistance the electric motor must give if this sensor fails heavy steering warning lights no power assist 3 assembly intermediate shaft sensor housing this is the mechanical link between the steering wheel and the steering gear it transfers motion from driver input to the steering rack while sensors collect data think of it as the bridge between driver force and electric assist 4 electric motor this is the heart of eps instead of hydraulic pressure this motor creates steering assist benefits no oil no pump low maintenance more efficient works only when needed when you turn slowly more assist when you drive fast less assist for stability 5 ecu electronic control unit the brain of eps it receives signals from 1 torque sensor 2 vehicle speed sensor 3 motor feedback then it calculates and commands how much assist when to cut assist safety shutdown if theres a failure ecu is why eps can integrate with abs stability control lane assist and parking assist 6 steering gear rack and pinion this converts rotational movement into linear movement to turn the wheels even without power assist the rack still works mechanically eps simply makes it easier if wear happens here rattling free play poor wheel alignment 7 vehicle speed sensor critical sensor that tells ecu how fast the vehicle is moving low speed more steering assist easy parking high speed reduced assist more control less wobble if this fails eps feels weird sometimes too light or too heavy why eps is the future of steering saves fuel no hydraulic leaks compatible with adas autonomous driving can selfcorrect steering lightweight and efficient

why batteries lose charge over time a key culprit found researchers have identified a key mechanism behind longterm battery degradation shedding light on why batteries gradually lose capacity even under normal use the findings could help extend battery life across consumer electronics and electric vehicles the study focuses on how batteries repeatedly expand and contract as ions move through electrode materials during charging cycles this mechanical stress often described as the battery breathing contributes to microscopic damage that accumulates over time especially under fast charging and high temperatures the discovery matters now because battery longevity increasingly determines the cost and sustainability of electrification longerlasting batteries reduce replacement needs lower lifecycle emissions and improve the economics of electric vehicles and gridscale storage historically battery improvements have come from incremental advances in materials manufacturing and software controls understanding degradation pathways enables better design choices smarter charging strategies and improved warranties translating laboratory insights into massproduced cells remains the next challenge what should manufacturers prioritize most faster charging lower cost or longer battery life
